source.title: Scale out for large minibatch SGD: Residual network training on ImageNet-1K with improved accuracy and reduced time to train
source.authors: V. Codreanu; Damian Podareanu; V. Saletore

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies global batch size and training choices and reports ImageNet validation accuracy, a different measure from the claim’s training–test error gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports large-batch validation results and experiments changing weight decay. It does not report random-label fitting, training error, or a direct train–test gap. Comparisons in Table X are cited literature, not this study’s results. Table I’s two accuracy pairs cannot be reliably assigned to the two learning-rate schedules from the supplied flattened table.
record.test_reason: The study varies global batch size in synchronous SGD and measures ImageNet validation accuracy, directly testing V5's held-out-performance claim. Tables II and IV contain fixed-epoch comparisons omitted from the record; training error or a train–test gap is not required by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that adapted training recipes enable fast, competitive large-batch ResNet-50 training, while accuracy still declines beyond a batch-size limit. They also report improved single-model accuracy and a 77.5% snapshot-ensemble result within a 120-epoch training budget.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synchronous SGD on ImageNet-1K ResNet-50 with linear learning-rate scaling and warm-up, while adding learning-rate schedule changes, batch-normalization adjustments, dynamic weight decay, and collapse phases.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports validation accuracy changes with batch size, weight decay, collapse, learning-rate schedules, warm-up, and batch-normalization settings. It states that accuracy degrades as batch size increases over a certain limit.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch 4096, reducing weight decay raises top-1 accuracy from 75.8% to 76.22%; adding the collapse recipe raises it to 76.65%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-decay and final-collapse choices can improve ImageNet accuracy at a fixed batch size.

record.code_released: https://github.com/intel/caffe (authors say models and scripts will be pushed there)
record.problems: No random-label or training-error results, no direct train–test gap measurement, and no matched smaller-batch control for the large-batch runs. The 65536-batch experiment uses a distinct schedule. The paper describes weight-decay and collapse effects empirically and does not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table I compares learning-rate schedules, but the flattened table does not identify which accuracy pair belongs to which schedule; excluded rather than assigning values. Table X reports comparisons to prior work, not this study’s own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Language models; a controlled small-batch reference for the very-large-batch adapted recipes; isolated effects of warmup, normalization and collapse on the batch penalty. The paper does not isolate longer training as a remedy at fixed batch and recipe.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Fixed-90-epoch batch comparisons: 8192 gives 75.81/92.93%, 12288 gives 75.25/92.90%, and 11520 gives 75.03/92.69%. These directly bear on the batch penalty.

Fixed-budget short-run comparisons: at 29 epochs on 256 nodes, batches 2048 and 8192 give 72.43/91.45% and 73.21/91.58%; at 37 epochs, batches 4096 and 8192 give 74.05/92.12% and 73.92/91.83%. Another batch-8192 run on 512 nodes gives 73.78/91.78% at 37 epochs.

Fixed-50-epoch Skylake results: batch 6400 gives 73.94/92.03% on 800 CPUs; batch 8192 gives 74.11/92.14% on 512 CPUs and 74.01/92.03% on 1024 CPUs. These show similar performance across this range, with hardware and local-batch differences.

Table X includes this study's own batch-8K accuracy of 76.6%, alongside its larger-batch results. The entire table should not be dismissed as cited literature; the 8K result lacks an explicit epoch budget in that table.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. Replace the record's unsupported limits_scope labels: lack of a matched control is an evidential limitation, not itself a finding against the claim. The supplied text contains fixed-epoch comparisons, contrary to the record's gate note. Recipe improvements at one fixed batch size do not independently demonstrate closure of a batch-size penalty.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No fixed-epoch comparison against a smaller-batch run with the same model and other settings; no training error or direct generalization-gap measurement. The 65536-batch run used a distinct schedule.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.baseline: 75.8% with weight decay 0.0001 and no collapse
rows.note: The authors report this change improves accuracy; it does not directly measure the batch-size gap.

rows.subject: ResNet-50

rows.check: The combined recipe improves accuracy at fixed batch 4096, without measuring a batch-size penalty. Table VIII prints initial weight decay 0.0005, but Sections V-B and VI consistently specify 0.00005 followed by 0.0001; flag this internal discrepancy.
